gap: No result ChatGPT got states that UGREEN's own NAS store sells the DXP4800 Plus and the US3000 120 W DC UPS as one bundle at $689.99 (and the DXP2800 + UPS at $449.99), or that the US3000 is not compatible with the DXP6800 and DXP8800 series, so it fits only the 2- and 4-bay NASync models.
standout_why: ChatGPT's answers cited nothing. I compared against its top results. qnap.com/en/solution/plex-best-nas says nothing about a UPS, power outages or bundles. The support.plex.tv articles are about transcoding and CPUs. terabytewise.com/best-nas-for-plex-transcoding has part of it: its product listings show NAS + UPS bundles at retailer prices ('DXP4800 Plus & US3000 ... Bundle' $692.53, 'DXP2800 & US2000 ... Bundle' $460.22) and the US2000's list of compatible models. Its article text never discusses a UPS. It does not give UGREEN's own bundle prices, and it does not say the US3000 excludes the 6- and 8-bay models.
kit_items: NAS: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus (4 bays, Intel Pentium Gold 8505, 10GbE). It is ChatGPT's 'best overall' pick, it is already in the Dealectric catalog under cj:ugreen, and UGREEN sells it bundled with a UPS. The DXP2800 (2 bays, N100) is the budget alternative and has its own UPS bundle.

Battery backup: UGREEN NAS UPS US3000 (120 W DC, 12,000 mAh, switches to battery in 0 s, USB-C to the NAS for monitoring). It is made for NASync, but it is listed as not compatible with the DXP6800 and DXP8800, so the kit must use a 2- or 4-bay model.
Drives: NAS-rated CMR HDDs. No approved brand store sells them, so they only fit in an Amazon cart, and I could not price them on Amazon today (see unsourced).
